scope: Read-only native investigation of selected generic component tick physical destruction monitors; no source or Ghidra edits in this follow-up.
limitation: Static native evidence only. No live ownership witness or exhaustive indirect-call closure. Destructor monitors alone are not proven sufficient for resumable holds, prerequisite topology mutation, earlier derived-component teardown, logical destruction callbacks, or arbitrary external writes. EBOOT.elf is separate and was not used.
findings: Common tick destructor142157BC0 changes vtable, unregisters at level+48 if tick+C bit40, then frees tick+20 backing; no retained-task wait.

Component base destructor1403AF1B0 frees component allocations at+1B8,+1A8,+198,+178,+168 before common tick destructor(component+110). Scene component1403AF4B0 tears down additional state before component base. A mutex first acquired at common tick dtor cannot detect these earlier destructor intervals.

UWorld destructor1421B4E60 is the before-entry physical teardown boundary; wrapper1421B5AE0 calls it then frees allocation when flags&1. Embedded world ticks are destructed only after several earlier world arrays are freed.

Prerequisite AddTickFunctionPrerequisite142159B90 and Remove142164920->142164960 can reallocate prerequisite backing without tick destruction. QueueTickFunctionWithPrerequisitesForEpoch142163BA0 also prunes invalid entries.

Native replacement StaticAllocateObject_Internal140F8CB30 invokes existing object virtual slot0 before memset and reconstruction, as retained in rollback-g1-physical-lifetime-native-2026-09-23.json. This supports destruction coverage for normal replacement only; exact selected class deleting/nondeleting destructor entry remains needed before derived teardown.
Component callback141D43230 dereferences tick+50 and component+188 before helper141D2CAC0 checks object item flags0x30000000 and registration. These checks cannot substitute for physical lifetime.
GC lease is not a native object replacement barrier. A world physical destructor monitor does not cover logical world/component lifecycle changes or prerequisite mutations.
recommendation: For a bounded supported concrete component class, monitor the earliest verified deleting and nondeleting destructor entries used by its vtable/direct callers, plus world1421B4E60. Record in-progress destruction under shared monitor mutex before any native destructor work; reject admission if in progress and terminal before-entry if a retained hold exists. Forward native work without holding monitor mutex to avoid nested destructor/native wait deadlocks, with scope completion bookkeeping. Do not claim resumability until concrete class entry coverage, prerequisite mutation exclusion or safe copy/revalidation, and no held raw prerequisite-owner lifetime gaps are closed. A common tick destructor monitor remains useful terminal defense in depth but is insufficient by itself.

/* Summary: Dispatches a component tick through native liveness, registration, tick-type and owner
   time-dilation guards.
   
   Parameters:
   pTickFunction: process-local tick-function binding with target component at +0x50.
   flDeltaSeconds: engine interval delta in XMM1.
   nLevelTick: engine level-tick selector in R8D.
   
   Algorithm:
   1. Build a 12-byte local call context: tick-function pointer followed by level-tick selector.
   2. Read target component +0x188 bit 11 as the special level-tick admission flag.
   3. Call 141D2CAC0 with component, flag, delta, selector and address of local context.
   4. Return only after the complete guarded component call.
   
   Returns:
   Void.
   
   Source:
   Native assembly 141D43230..141D43269. Vtable slot +8 at 143865FA0, diagnostic-message slot
   141D41E40 emits [TickComponent]. Vtable 143865F98 is installed by 14237F8F0 and 141D31450.
   
   Replay relevance:
   Helper 141D2CAC0 validates UObject flags 0x30000000, invokes component virtual +0x350, checks
   +0x188 bit 0, resolves owner at +0x190, applies special level-tick rules, and scales delta by
   owner +0x80 or 1.0. It invokes component virtual +0x300 with the original tick-function pointer
   in R9. This includes derived particle fade, completion and destruction work; skipping it is not
   presentation-neutral. Any resumable host continuation must retain logical arguments and validated
   bindings, never this function's stack context.
   
   Special Cases:
   Incoming R9 and stack arguments are not consumed by this concrete implementation. The 12-byte
   local context is valid only for the synchronous helper call. local_28 is the outgoing
   fifth-argument slot, not retained state. Secondary/custom tick-function implementations and
   asynchronous component tasks require separate ownership audit. */

void DispatchComponentTickFunction(void *pTickFunction,float flDeltaSeconds,int nLevelTick)

{
  void *pDispatchTickFunction;
  int nDispatchLevelTick;
  
  pDispatchTickFunction = pTickFunction;
  nDispatchLevelTick = nLevelTick;
  FUN_141d2cac0(*(longlong *)((longlong)pTickFunction + 0x50),
                (byte)(*(uint *)(*(longlong *)((longlong)pTickFunction + 0x50) + 0x188) >> 0xb) & 1,
                flDeltaSeconds,nLevelTick,&pDispatchTickFunction);
  return;
}
